content: Everyone, based on the fact that many people (5DN1L and the general) think that this is a slightly harder version of Chapter 1, I will look to modify this contribution. However, please do not suggest anything as I will not review them.
I hope you received enough feedback from the community to improve your contribution. Once you have made the necessary updates, publish your contribution!

Looking at the author's solutions, I think this reinforces the point made earlier that Chapters 1 and 2 are essentially the same puzzle.

The Chapter 2 solution is almost identical to the Chapter 1 ( https://www.codingame.com/contribute/view/1457103173fc1ac09f804c82de3e771810baa8 ) solution. The logic for evaluating each gate has been copied verbatim; the only substantial addition is a loop that repeatedly applies the same gate-evaluation logic to a running value.

In other words, solving Chapter 2 already requires implementing everything from Chapter 1. The difference is not the introduction of a new concept, but simply applying the same concept multiple times.

Because of that, I still think Chapters 1 and 2 would work better as a single puzzle, potentially reclassified as a clash of code. The progression from evaluating one gate to evaluating a sequence of gates is too minor to justify a separate chapter on its own.

There's also a pending clash of code on the theme of bitwise operations awaiting approval: https://www.codingame.com/contribute/view/148614f05c804fa2b7058d9f5aa1bc4315fed4 . In my view, your puzzles are of a similar difficulty level, so it'd make more sense to combine them into a single Clash of Code rather than split them across multiple chapters.

Great Puzzle for learning about logic Gates!
I am not sure I would classify this as a medium puzzle, as it was rather easy for me. However, it’s probably more challenging if you don’t already have some knowledge about logic gates.  
Furthermore, it has great potential to make much harder puzzles, with multiple inputs and multiple lines of Gates.
